description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-libraries-spec §4.7.1 — what an `operator_compose` entry MERGED, and which spelling of a bare-name match SURVIVES. Step 5 used to make silence normative: an entry that merged everything and one that merged nothing produced the same observable outcome, so a document could integrate a private decoupled operator while the mechanism got no contribution at all, and the only evidence was a state count one too high. Three things are pinned here and they are DISTINCT. (1) The merge TALLY is reported: `operator_compose_no_merge` when nothing landed, `operator_compose_partial_merge` when only some did, both naming the unmatched dependent variables. These are WARNINGS, on measured evidence rather than taste — 19 entries in this repository's own corpus zero-merge today and 1 merges partially, every one of them spec-valid under step 5 (a transport operator whose only equation defines its own wind field has no tendency to contribute), so promoting them would reject documents the format grants. (2) `require_match: true` is the author's opt-in that promotes either to a hard refusal, `operator_compose_require_match_unmatched`; a PARTIAL match refuses exactly as a zero match does, and `require_match_satisfied` is the non-vacuity anchor proving the flag is not simply always-fatal. (3) The BARE-NAME fallback's surviving spelling follows the state's OWNER — the component the document declares first — not `systems[0]`; the `owner_rename_*` trio is what pins that an entry means the same thing in either argument order. Like `override_key_diagnostics`, this category compares DIAGNOSTIC OUTCOMES rather than numbers, so it carries no golden: each binding's own suite asserts its idiomatic warning channel and error type per case. The `owner_rename_*` cases additionally pin two VALUES — the surviving state's name and its default — because the whole defect is that those two, and nothing else, changed with argument order.

diagnostic_surface._comment: The idiomatic channel each binding reports a WARNING on, and the idiomatic error each raises for the `require_match` refusal. The TYPE and CHANNEL are per-language; the OUTCOME classification and the diagnostic CODE are the cross-binding contract. No binding's `flatten` signature carries a diagnostic slot, so the warning goes to whatever stream that language's callers already watch.

warning_channel.rust: eprintln!("warning: …") — the pushdown_rewrite residual-diagnostic idiom — with the side-effect-free `capture_coupling_diagnostics` counterpart for tests
warning_channel.go: the package-level couplingWarnf hook, defaulting to os.Stderr

cases.note: The issue's Symptom 2, verbatim. Two states where the author meant one; the operator integrates a private decoupled decay. Step 5 still preserves the equation — that half is unchanged — but it is no longer silent.
The seven-of-twelve-species shape reduced to one-of-two. `Chem.O3` gains the deposition term; the operator's CO tendency lands nowhere and survives decoupled.

Same document as `no_merge`, with `require_match: true`. Refused at FLATTEN, not at validate: the document is schema-valid and structurally valid, and only the merge knows the answer. Same placement rule as coupling/couple_multiplicative_no_tendency.esm.

A PARTIAL match refuses exactly as a zero match does. There is no 'some is enough' reading an author could rely on — an operator reaching seven of twelve species and silently missing five is the defect the flag exists to catch.
NON-VACUITY ANCHOR. Without it, a binding that refused every `require_match` entry — or that warned on every compose — would pass every other case in this category.

The issue's Symptom 1 document verbatim. `Sink` is declared first, so `Sink.O3` owns the unified state and its 40.0 is the surviving initial condition. Pairs with `owner_rename_mechanism_listed_first`, which is the SAME document with only `systems` reversed and MUST agree.

THE ORDER-INDEPENDENCE PIN. Identical models in identical declaration order; ONLY the `systems` array is reversed. Before this change it produced `Chem.O3` at 30.0 instead — an argument order silently choosing which of two initial conditions survived. A binding that still renames onto `systems[0]` fails exactly here. The merged tendency is arithmetically identical in both fixtures; only the term ORDER differs, which §4.7.1 step 4 fixes as `rhs_A + factor * rhs_B` and this category does not pin.

DECLARATION order decides, not argument order: the operator is still listed first in `systems`, but the mechanism is declared first and keeps its name and its 30.0. This is the reseact.esm shape — an operator-first coupling entry over a mechanism declared above it — where the old rule moved the mechanism's states out from under every downstream reference to them. It is also what makes the previous case non-trivial: the two differ only in `models` order, so a binding that hard-coded either answer fails one of them.
